passes.result: Cancelled reads waiting for session refresh. Previously a discarded request waited for the shared refresh (up to its 10-second timeout). `deduplicatedRefresh` now accepts an optional AbortSignal and cancels the waiter while retaining the shared refresh for other requests. Cleanup removes listeners when refresh settles. Tests cover concurrent retained/discarded waiters and pre-aborted callers. A controlled 100 ms refresh with cancellation at 5 ms settled 0.055 ms after abort, compared with 95.202 ms before (20 samples). This is cancellation latency, not page load time.

Obsolete request dispatch and decoding. `wikiReadHttp` checks cancellation before dispatch, after refresh, and after body decoding. A stale query cannot start another GET or validate/publish a late body. The regression test deliberately finishes a body after abort and verifies its Zod transform never runs. This avoids extra requests and unnecessary validation work during navigation/session changes.

Cancellation across all read families. Added optional signals to identity, Drive-list, preferences, metadata-icon, sort-order, and document-alias reads. Updated identity and alias hooks; agent 2 updated the sidebar hooks in its own scope. The remaining direct TanStack query callbacks were converted to explicit signal-forwarding wrappers, preserving existing positional arguments and preventing the query context from accidentally being passed as an AbortSignal.

Terminal refresh failure fast path. A denied refresh now returns the established expired-session error immediately. It no longer attempts to decode the already-cancelled initial 401 body. The unauthorized notification still fires once, and unavailable refreshes remain retryable 503 errors without clearing the user session. Tests exercise both failure classes.

Parallel expired-session recovery. Verified two independently started reads produce two initial GETs, one shared refresh, and one replay per GET. The cancellation variant verifies only the retained read replays. Retained the shared refresh design rather than aborting it when one observer disappears, which would break other active reads.

Streaming BFF response. Added a stream regression that supplies an upstream body without EOF. The route returns headers before the body finishes and subsequently decodes the complete body correctly. Retained direct authorized body streaming; buffering or another JSON/Flight serialization would reintroduce a loading barrier and allocations.

Read-route coverage and disconnect propagation. Exercised all 13 allowed paths, including search/snippets and every extras family. Existing tests cover write/unknown-path rejection, cookie protection, no-store responses, and error redaction. Added a disconnect test showing abort reaches the pending upstream fetch. Retained the route's request-plus-timeout cancellation and restricted path list.

Bootstrap deadline measurement. Controlled-clock tests verify fresh identity recovery begins at 1,500 ms and two stalled reads settle by a combined 3,000 ms. Retained the streaming shell and bounded preload instead of waiting indefinitely for Drive. A successful bootstrap continues to avoid a second identity request.

Avoid an unsafe bootstrap shortcut. Reviewed skipping `/auth/me` after a bootstrap 401. Rejected it: `backend/app/drive/dependencies.py` can return 401 for missing Google credentials while the app identity remains authenticated. The new regression confirms a fresh identity read still succeeds in this case. Browser-cached profiles and broader authenticated response caching were also rejected because they undermine identity isolation and revocation checks.

Remove repeated bootstrap validation and DRY transforms. `zBootstrapRead` already validates every nested resource. Extracted shared pure transforms for Drive summaries, icons, preferences, profile, and sort order; standalone resource schemas retain their wire validation while bootstrap maps its already-validated data directly. This extends the first tranche's nested-tree improvement to the other metadata arrays. Tests preserve default values, nullable fields, and rejection of malformed nested data. A 1,409,370-byte fixture with 100 drives and 10,000 each of document icons, folder icons, and sort orders has deeply equal before/after output: median 4.190 → 1.407 ms (66.4% less CPU), p95 7.302 → 3.365 ms, 100 samples. The fixture has no tree, so the result isolates this additional metadata improvement. Converted wire-property reads to bracket access and constant-backed test/query keys so strict lint and Prettier agree without additional suppressions.

File action menu initialization. Every file/folder action menu previously initialized rename, delete, and copy mutation observers and closed dialog trees. Extracted `item-menu-actions.tsx`; `ItemMenu` keeps its native accessible dropdown trigger and loads/mounts actions through `next/dynamic` only after first opening. Actions remain mounted afterward. A 500-trigger regression renders zero mutation hook calls, eliminating 1,500 initial action observers for that case. Enter-key opening and selecting Rename verify that its dialog survives dropdown dismissal.

Create menu initialization. Extracted `create-file-menu-actions.tsx`, preserving Smart Create, Markdown import, Google file types, defaults, destinations, and mutation behavior. The trigger lazily loads/mounts the body on first opening and retains it afterward. A 500-trigger check creates zero create-mutation observers. Enter-key opening and choosing Doc show the `New Doc` dialog with `Untitled Doc` after the menu closes.

Emoji picker theme/client subscriptions. Initial rows previously subscribed each closed picker to theme/client state and initialized a transition. These hooks now initialize only on first picker opening. The controlled Popover and existing focus primitive are retained. Tests confirm no theme subscription before opening.

Document/folder icon mutation observers. Removed unconditional icon mutation hooks from `FileRow` and `TreeNode`. `PickableIcon` passes an explicit typed document/folder target; the corresponding existing mutation hook initializes inside the opened picker body. Existing optimistic mutation logic, target IDs, error toasts, shortcut restrictions, and read-only restrictions are preserved. The body stays mounted after first opening; a pending-change regression verifies that closing/reopening retains its busy state and prevents a second concurrent icon change. Only the selected target's hook initializes.

Closed Drive access sheets. Moved permissions query initialization, page flattening, deduplication, and sorting into content mounted by the Sheet primitive only when opened. Closed drives create no permissions observers and derive no unused lists. Opening still requests the exact drive with fresh permissions and the established access UI. The native Sheet opening regression verifies the drive ID and enabled query state.

Collapsed folder and Drive derivation. Collapsed folders still display their visible child count but skip child object construction, sorting, optimistic ordering, and sortable IDs. Collapsed Drive roots skip unused root sorting and optimistic derivation. The 10,000-child folder test retains its count and performs zero locale comparisons. Expanded ordering, shortcut handling, lazy file loading, drop targets, and node accessibility remain intact.

Repeated metadata hints during navigation. Added a WeakMap cache containing only the last metadata lookup per immutable query array. Initial lookups keep the existing early-exit scan; repeated hits and misses avoid rescanning large arrays. Array replacement invalidates the hint naturally, and eviction/session replacement does not retain arrays. Existing shortcut timestamp rules are preserved. A synthetic 10,000-node repeated final-node lookup measured a median of 0.030093 ms for the linear reference versus 0.000193 ms for the cached helper (25 samples, 1,000 iterations each). Immutable data replacement tests confirm current names replace cached hints. Results: `/private/tmp/sarj-wiki-perf-sidebar-cache-benchmark.json`.

Global sidebar request cancellation. Coordinated with agent 1's optional AbortSignal read API additions. Drives, preferences, folder icons, document icons, and sort orders now forward the TanStack Query signal explicitly instead of passing the entire query context as a positional argument. A real hook/provider regression verifies five AbortSignals and their cancellation on unmount. Existing tree/permissions/file/folder query gates remain unchanged. Renamed `use-wiki-tree.test.ts` to `.tsx` to run the hook harness with JSX.

Constrained folder hover speculation. Folder hover reads now use the same reusable-speculation policy as Drive navigation: hidden pages and save-data connections avoid unused background reads, and touch hover does not start prefetching. Direct expansion remains ungated and immediately loads requested content. Parameterized native event tests verify one healthy hover read and zero hidden/save-data/touch reads.

Cold overlay index allocation. Replaced `new Map(items.map(...))` in the shared index builder with direct insertion. This preserves key/value and duplicate-key semantics while avoiding a transient mapped array and one tuple per entry. The local 10,000-overlay benchmark measured 0.506167 ms for tuple mapping versus 0.261459 ms for direct insertion (50 samples after warmup, approximately 48% less CPU for this cold builder). Existing immutable shared-index tests pass. Results: `/private/tmp/sarj-wiki-perf-sidebar-map-benchmark.json`.

Repeated deferred-dialog state updates. The shared deferred-dialog hook returns its existing state when the requested open state is already current. Duplicate close notifications no longer allocate state or rerender mounted action/picker bodies. The monotonic first-mount behavior and pending/recovery state remain intact. Existing menu/create/picker lifecycle and index tests passed again after this change.

Collation candidate retained. Measured replacing default `localeCompare` with a cached `Intl.Collator().compare` for a 10,000-name sort containing ASCII and international names. The current comparator was faster: 0.633542 ms versus 2.077458 ms (25 samples). Retained the existing locale behavior and faster implementation.

Viewer pool and warmup candidate retained. Reviewed viewer ownership, HTML content version requirements, iframe reuse, warmup count, and strong-intent metadata authorization. The existing pool is capped at three documents and idle warmup at one, with constrained-device safeguards. Increasing speculation or the pool would add competing Google/iframe work, while removing fresh metadata authorization would weaken permissions. Existing viewer store, host, intent, and warmup tests passed; retained these limits.

Tree virtualization/context candidate retained. Reviewed the remaining per-row native tree and drag subscriptions. Replacing live rows or blanket containment without browser traces would affect measured drag geometry, keyboard focus, accessible menus, and nested folder targets. React Compiler, shared immutable indexes, memoized rows, selective drag/move stores, and the new closed-content deferral already remove avoidable derivation. Retained native tree rendering rather than adding unmeasured structural complexity or a new dependency under the current scope. Large real-workspace browser traces are the appropriate next evidence for that separate change.
